subject: learning/forgejo-fast-installed-feature-e2e
statement: The opt-in Forgejo feature E2E installs actual source-built Pyxis binaries into isolated temporary directories, reuses an existing Forgejo repository, and stubs only the implementation and review model processes. Git, task projection, confinement, feature tests, native comments, exact-head local status, draft PR publication, review evidence, and repeat-run idempotency remain real.
intent: Provide a fast, reusable feature-development regression that can catch installed-flow and provider wiring failures without paying model latency or creating a new repository on every run.
rationale: A fake GitHub transport or in-process CLI call cannot prove the advertised install and native Forgejo path. Deterministic model helpers remove the slow nondeterministic dependency while retaining the real boundaries under test. The fixture seeds a failing feature test, initializes with local tasks before switching to Forgejo to avoid shared onboarding writes, uses unique owned refs and labels including all three review stores, and isolates HOME/ZDOTDIR/XDG directories to protect the user's shell setup.
fit_criterion: TestLiveForgejoInstalledFeatureDevelopment proves the feature test fails before implementation and passes after one implementation plus one review, publishes a draft PR and review at the verified head, and reruns without additional model calls, PRs, comments, or statuses. Cleanup closes owned work, removes owned refs/labels, and verifies pre-existing remote state is preserved. Local CI keeps this E2E fast; real Forgejo Actions runner behavior remains a separate verification boundary.
